Chapter Two: Encounters with the Wider World.
Leaving home for the very first time—there’s nothing quite like it, is there? It’s exciting, sure, but it can also be downright scary. Imagine this: a young man, now with a family of his own, is sent off to study law in a faraway land. His destination? England. And the journey ahead is packed with uncertainty—new customs to learn, faces he doesn’t recognize, and the weight of high expectations.
Before he left, he made a heartfelt promise to his mother: he’d stay true to their family values, steering clear of meat, alcohol, and other temptations. That promise becomes his anchor, guiding every choice he makes.
Stepping into London feels like landing on another planet compared to the quiet town he left behind. The city is alive, buzzing with energy, but there’s also this undercurrent of loneliness. He tries to fit in, but it’s tough—his traditional clothes make him feel out of place, and he’s unsure about all the new social customs swirling around him.
He’s fascinated by the idea of becoming a true “gentleman.” Maybe, just maybe, a polished appearance will earn him the respect he craves. So, he dives in—buys new clothes, signs up for dance lessons, even practices public speaking. But no matter what he tries, that sense of truly belonging always seems just out of reach.
Even something as simple as food turns into a daily hurdle. Vegetarianism is rare in London, and friends encourage him to break his promise. But he stands firm, searching the city for vegetarian restaurants and suitable meals. In these small, stubborn acts, he stumbles into a community of others who share his values. Over shared meals and honest conversations, he discovers that you really can live by your principles—even when the world around you says otherwise.
Books quickly become his closest companions. He reads everything he can get his hands on—religious texts, philosophy, even books about diet and health. What fascinates him most is the wisdom woven through so many different faiths: compassion, self-control, the quest for truth. These ideas spark a habit of questioning and deep reflection that will shape his whole life.
Being an outsider makes him notice things he never saw before—like how people are treated differently because of how they look, talk, or where they come from. For the first time, he really sees what prejudice and injustice look like. And from that experience, empathy begins to take root—especially for those who are misunderstood or pushed aside.
After finishing his studies, he returns home. But life doesn’t magically get easier. The world of law isn’t simple; clients are hard to find, and the courtroom is intimidating. Speaking up feels overwhelming, and he sometimes loses his train of thought. The fear of failure is real—but so is his determination to keep going.
Family life brings its own set of challenges. Tradition pulls in one direction, while personal growth tugs in another. He and his wife work through misunderstandings and learn to balance the demands of extended family. Through it all, the value of honesty, patience, and genuine respect becomes clearer than ever.
Then, out of the blue, an opportunity comes up—work in South Africa. It’s a place far from everything familiar, but it’s full of possibility. Deciding to go isn’t easy, but in the end, necessity and curiosity win out.
This move isn’t just a change of scenery—it’s the start of a brand-new chapter. One that’ll test every lesson he’s learned so far, and demand even more courage and conviction than before.
